key_insight: For the Poisson problem on convex polyhedral domains, the analyzed DG methods achieve optimal discrete W^{1,p} error estimates and conjugate-exponent inf-sup stability without logarithmic factors for 1/(1−ε) < p < 1/ε, with fixed ε ∈ (0, 1/2).
engineering_relevance: These guarantees support reliable gradient approximation and stability assessment for DG discretizations of elliptic PDEs used in computational engineering.
method: Analyze symmetric IPDG, hybrid mixed DG, and two representative HDG methods.
Combine interface Green’s functions with new Fubini-type weighted estimates.
Use inf-sup stability and a dual problem to extend estimates below p = 2.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical error and stability guarantees, illustrated by one numerical example.
watch_item: Results assume convex polyhedral domains; the extension to polyhedral meshes excludes the hybrid mixed DG method.
paper_title: $W^{1,p}$ error estimates of an IPDG and a class of HDG methods for the Poisson problem on convex polyhedral domains
